headline: Amblyotube VR app treats lazy eye with YouTube content, saves 95% on therapy
summary: Seven Sports' Amblyotube uses Meta Quest's dual eyepieces for dichoptic training, converting regular YouTube videos into an interactive visual workout for users aged 13 and up.
details: Seven Sports has launched Amblyotube, a new Meta Quest app designed to treat amblyopia (lazy eye) and improve visual coordination. The app claims to offer a 95% saving compared to other amblyopia treatment apps.

Amblyotube leverages the Meta Quest's independent eyepieces to deliver dichoptic training, sending separate video feeds to each eye simultaneously. This unique VR capability transforms passive screen time into active visual therapy.

Upon first launch, users select their weaker eye, which is crucial for accurate training. The app offers Mild, Moderate, or Severe presets, or an internal LogMAR vision check to automatically adjust the treatment profile.

The innovative aspect is its ability to convert standard YouTube content into a "visual gym," providing engaging, active training. This approach contrasts sharply with designs intended to maximize user retention.

Recommended usage is 30-40 minutes daily, up to one hour, for users aged 13 and above. It functions as an assistive tool for visual training and depth perception, not a diagnostic, therapeutic, or curative medical device.

headline_marked: [[Harvest time-tracking service gutted]] after Bending Spoons acquisition, prices soar 900%
headline: Harvest time-tracking service gutted after Bending Spoons acquisition, prices soar 900%
summary: Harvest, a popular time-tracking and invoicing tool, has drastically increased its monthly fees from $13.32 to $133.98 for existing users following its 2025 acquisition by Bending Spoons, known for gutting Vimeo.
details: Harvest was a beloved time-tracking and invoicing service, praised for its simple, reliable interface and reasonable pricing. It focused on solving a specific problem without scope creep, making it ideal for self-employed contractors.
The company was acquired in 2025 by Bending Spoons, a firm with a reputation for overhauling acquired services, notably Vimeo. This acquisition raised initial concerns among its user base.

Post-acquisition, Harvest moved users to a new "enterprise" plan, hiking monthly prices from $13.32 to $133.98 – a tenfold increase. A new "flex" plan, while cheaper, adds a 2% skim on top of standard transaction fees.

Users attempting to contact customer support about these changes reported encountering Large Language Model responses instead of human interaction. This indicates a significant shift in customer service approach.

The drastic changes and perceived "enshittification" have led long-time users to seek alternative invoicing and bookkeeping solutions. The situation highlights concerns about private equity acquisitions of popular software services.
